Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ea62933c2239b4c35b675f6af7d6812e01173edc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4b4df50a303cf4dee4ff4d14a070bd6b22b5179c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/qa/scenarios/src/schema.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/loader.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/orchestrate.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/prompts.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/namespace.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/test/refusals.test.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/test/runner/units.test.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/test/runner/orchestrate.test.ts, docs/qa/scenarios/asset_lifecycle.json, docs/qa/scenarios/crm_account_with_contacts.json, docs/qa/scenarios/invoice_with_line_items.json, docs/qa/scenarios/leave_balances.json, docs/qa/scenarios/order_to_cash.json, docs/qa/scenarios/project_with_tasks.json, docs/qa/scenarios/requisition_to_receipt.json, docs/qa/scenarios/service_desk.json, docs/qa/scenarios/travel_expense.json, docs/qa/scenarios/README.md, packages/qa/scenarios/README.md, .changeset/30914-scenario-card-person-fields.md + packages/qa/scenarios/src/index.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/index.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/tsup.config.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/package.json, packages/qa/scenarios/src/export/record.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/scorecard.ts

Face: narrowing. `reviewFace` returns no path hit for the 20 files (`record-recognisers --template --paths` says the paths decide no face and the changeset's `Clause-②:` line decides); the changeset and PR body both carry `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, which the recogniser reads as the narrowing face. `@objectstack/scenarios` is published since PR #31221 and its `.` entry (`src/index.ts`) re-exports `schema.ts` and `loader.ts`, so the card schema and the loader's accept set are published; `./runner` (`src/runner/index.ts`) re-exports `orchestrate.ts`, `prompts.ts` and `namespace.ts`. Read against `main` at the head's check-run time: base `bdefd49f`, PR base ref `ea62933c`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **S2, handle fields declared (schema.ts, loader.ts, prompts.ts) — right.** `run.userHandleFields: FieldRef[]`, optional, `min(1)`, on the published `ScenarioCardSchema`. `userHandleFields` in `prompts.ts` is now one line over the declaration and infers nothing (main's version walked every direct scope rule not in lookups/selects). The loader refuses, each with a named path and reason: a scope rule whose terminal field is none of `id`, a declared lookup, a declared select or a declared handle (`checkPath` returns the hop list, the last pair is the terminal field, so `contact.account.owner` is judged as `account.owner` and `account.owner.team` as `employee.team`); and a handle declaration on the row id, a declared lookup, a declared select, an unseeded or unexpected object, a field no seed row carries (`checkField`), or a duplicate (`duplicates`). The handle block runs before the persona loop, so the scope check reads the full validated set. Twelve refusal pins plus the delete-the-declaration control pin each arm.
- **Handle set before and after — right.** Read off the nine head cards: main's inference rule (direct scope field, not `id`, not a declared lookup or select) yields `account.owner` on crm, `invoice.owner` on invoice, `task.assignee` on project and nothing on the other six; the declared set is exactly the same three. The units test loads the nine cards from `docs/qa/scenarios` with zero refusals and pins the three, and Test Core is green on this head.
- **S3, `personas[].record = { object, id }` (schema.ts, loader.ts) — right, including when it is required.** The S3 ruling (6707631426) says required for a persona with a scope, optional for a global one, refused when it names no seed row. Read alone, that would refuse the three control cards, whose scoped personas are users with no person row. The #30913 ruling (6707625367, Q1 = A′ item 5) keeps the `userHandleFields` route for crm, invoice and project so both models coexist. The dev's rule, required unless a direct scope rule on a declared handle field names the persona, is the only reading under which items 1 and 5 both hold, and on the nine cards it carves out exactly the three controls. The refusal for a record naming no seeded row reads the loader's `ids` map (seeded row ids per object), so an unseeded object fails the same way; both are pinned. `PERSON_USER_FIELD = 'user'` matches the ruling's "fixed by name, not chosen per card"; the runner does not read `record`, which is #30913's half as the ruling orders. Observation, no fix: the exemption does not check that the direct rule's value is this persona's own handle; today `personaHandles` binds every direct-scope string value to its persona, so it holds by construction.
- **Six cards filled — right.** asset_lifecycle employee e06 / dept_manager e05, leave_balances e07 / e05, order_to_cash e03 / e01, requisition_to_receipt e02 / e13, travel_expense e02 / e01, service_desk a02 / a04 / cus_03. Each id is the one the persona's `role` string already names, and each is a seeded row (the loader would have refused otherwise). Every scoped persona across the nine cards now names a person by record or by a direct handle rule; no global persona was given one, which the ruling leaves optional.
- **Run record `seed.rewritten` (orchestrate.ts `RunHalf.seed`, `seedApp`) — right.** Set only inside the user-handle branch, as sorted unique `object.field` of the namespaced card; pinned in two orchestrate tests (`democrm_account.owner`). The export side's `RunHalfSchema` in `src/export/record.ts` is a `z.looseObject` that does not model `seed`, so the new key passes through.
- **S1, per-turn `seedDependence` (loader.ts `truthsOver`, orchestrate.ts) — right.** `truthsOver(card, seed)` factors the loader's own resolver, in-scope test and withheld rule (`seedReader`, `withholds`, `truthReads`) and computes every truth over a given seed, with a `TruthError` read as "not defined" rather than refused. `seedDependence(scenario, refused)` keeps the row walk, computes the truths once over the seed less the out rows, and `question(q, persona)` compares that turn's truth to the loaded one with `JSON.stringify`; both sides come from the same `evaluateTruth` and the same `{ kind: 'withheld' }` literal, so key order is stable. `runHalf` asks it inside the persona loop. The reason text is new; nothing downstream parses it (`scorecard.ts` only tests presence, `record.ts` types it as a string). ct4 pin: units test and orchestrate test both show `contacts_per_account/sdr` measured and only `unattached_contacts` and `contacts_by_industry` out; the all-accounts-refused run keeps the three turns no account feeds, and the "not defined" arm (avg over no rows) is pinned.
- **Exports through `.` and `./runner` — right, and named.** Added through `.`: `truthsOver` (loader) and `PERSON_USER_FIELD` (schema); the `ScenarioCard` type widens by two optional keys. Through `./runner`: `seedDependence` changes its signature (`LoadedScenario` in place of the card; `question(q, persona)`), `RunHalf.seed` gains `rewritten`, `userHandleFields` keeps its signature with declared-only semantics. Nothing is removed or renamed. The changeset names the signature change and tells `seedDependence` callers what moves.
- **namespace.ts, 6 lines outside the claimed surface — right and necessary.** Without the two spreads the namespaced card keeps bare object names in `userHandleFields[].object` and `record.object`, so `userHandleFields` answers `account.owner` while the seed loop iterates `democrm_account`: the handle rewrite would silently stop for every run. The orchestrate test's `rewritten: ['democrm_account.owner']` depends on it.
- **Docs — right.** `docs/qa/scenarios/README.md` row 4 and the Personas section state both declarations and every new refusal; the package README states per-turn dependence, `truthsOver` and `seed.rewritten`.

### ② Semver level

`patch` is correct. Ruling A in `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` decouples the level from `Clause-②`: `Metadata-protocol: none` means every introduced entry is `patch`, full stop, and a `minor` beside `none` is refused. No platform schema key moves, the card format is QA tooling, so `none` is the right protocol line and the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` disposition is in the changeset. The BREAKING banner is present and names the loader's accept-set narrowing, which the `(narrowing)` arm requires. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is the right spelling for this diff: `yes` because a published schema and two published entries widen (two optional keys, `truthsOver`, `PERSON_USER_FIELD`), the `(narrowing)` arm because the loader refuses cards it accepted before and `./runner`'s `seedDependence` breaks at compile time for a caller; `record-recognisers` documents `yes (narrowing)` as owing the narrowing face. Check Changeset is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation 1, `namespace.ts` outside the claimed surface.** Answered: necessary, 6 lines, named in the PR body and here in ①. No escalation.
- **Deviation 2, `pr_create` sent no labels or assignees.** Not a contract matter; the seat applies labels at landing. No escalation.
- **Deviation 3, gate loop on `33a20989`, changeset gates and the dogfood battery re-run on `4b4df50a`.** The two heads differ by one sentence in the changeset (`4b4df50a` is a changeset-only commit), and the check-runs on `4b4df50a` are the gate verdicts: 48 check-runs, 35 success, 13 skipped, 0 failure, including Test Core with its 8 shards, Lint & Repo Gates (which runs the one locally not-measured `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`), Check Changeset, Type Check · workspace, PR-body guards and Governed Surface Queue Guard. Answered.
- **Report and PR-body claim "origin/main has moved two commits since, neither in `packages/qa/scenarios`" — stale, harmless; should-fix the wording or merge `origin/main` before landing.** `main` is 9 commits past base `bdefd49f`, and one, `d3b6ff43` (#31265, codex and external drivers), lands in `packages/qa/scenarios`: `runner/cli.ts`, `runner/driver.ts`, `runner/transcript.ts`, `runner/index.ts`, `export/record.ts`, `export/exporter.ts`, the package README. It merged at 21:08Z; this PR opened at 21:24Z and its check-runs started 21:24 to 21:38Z, so CI judged a merge that already held it, GitHub reports `mergeable: true, clean`, and none of those files reads `seedDependence`, `question`, `userHandleFields` or `RunHalf.seed` (the record schema is loose). The serial note on #31159 (`driver.ts`, `cli.ts`) holds: this PR touches neither.
- **Live model run and recorded replay not measured** (maintainer pause; no recording in the container). The per-turn rule is pinned on the real crm card through the fake-app `runCard` tests. Accepted as stated.
- No open questions, no security findings, no out-of-scope findings in the report.

### ④ Design judgment

- **Loud at authoring time.** Every new acceptance condition is a load-time refusal with an exact path and a message that names the remedy (`list it in run.userHandleFields when the value is a handle … or declare it in expect.lookups or expect.selectFields`; `add record: { object, id } … or scope it by a direct rule on a declared user-handle field`). Nothing is tolerated and corrected at run time: `userHandleFields` cannot answer a field the card did not declare, and a card with a scope rule on an undeclared text field, the exact mis-seed S2 names, is refused before any build. Deleting the crm declaration produces three refusals, two on the scope rules and one on the missing person, which is the right amount of noise.
- **Structurally harder to get wrong for an AI-authored card.** A card must now say, in the card, what each scope value names, and the loader cross-checks the claim against the seed (the field exists, is not a row id, lookup or select, is not declared twice) and against the personas (a scoped persona is a seed row or a handle). The `strictObject` on `record` refuses stray keys. The one remaining inference, which persona a handle text belongs to, stays as it was and is #30913's half.
- **The narrowing against the published spec on `main`.** It takes away exactly the tolerated inference, not a declared capability: every card that loaded on `main` with a declared meaning still loads, and the nine open cards load unchanged with the same three rewritten fields. The per-turn dependence rule removes an over-wide not-measured, grades more of what the run can grade, and never grades a turn whose truth the refused row moved, so it cannot produce a new false fail.
- **Nothing speculative beyond the card's asks.** `truthsOver` is the mechanism S1 asks for ("re-evaluating each question's truth over the seed minus the out rows") and is factored from the loader rather than duplicated; `PERSON_USER_FIELD` is the ruling's "fixed by name" made a constant for #30913 to read; the namespace change is a consequence, not a feature. The terminal-field reading of a path rule is a judgment call the PR states; the alternative (direct rules only) would leave a path ending on an undeclared field to inference, which S2 exists to remove, so the stricter reading is the right one.
